Enterprise: Verisk Analytics (VRSK) — post-divestiture pure-play data,
analytics and technology provider to the global P&C insurance industry.
FYE 2025-12-31.

Archetype: B — Quality Compounder.
Valuation engine: Engine 1 — Traditional DCF + Multiples.
Why not another engine?
- The company is asset-light, cash-generative, high incremental-return;
  it is not an option-led/expectation story requiring Engine 4.
- It is not materially cyclical in the Engine-2 sense: 83% of revenue is

- It is now a single reporting segment (Insurance), not a hardware-plus-
  platform hybrid requiring Engine 3.

the divestiture generated roughly $41M adjusted EBITDA before corporate
allocations per the NTB press release, announcing entity: Verisk/TransUnion

smaller analytics vendors and in-house actuarial teams are already
integrated. Because loss-cost data quality is a network/regulatory asset,
price competition is limited; the larger effect is carrier in-sourcing until

Reflexivity: High stock price helps VRSK retain/hire AI talent through
stock comp and lets it repurchase fewer shares at better prices. Low price
would not impair customer contracts. Reflexivity is modestly positive but
not first-order.
Customer evolution: Carriers have been consolidating. VRSK’s counteraction
is per-claim/transaction pricing and AI modules that increase revenue per
seat. Late-adopter risk: small insurers still using legacy methods will
eventually be acquired by larger carriers or become VRSK clients.

Range:
- 50% CI: $185–$250.
- 80% CI: $155–$280.

■ SECTION 7. RISKS & CATALYSTS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Risks:
1. Organic growth does not re-accelerate to 6% in H2-2026. Q1-2026 OCC
   was 4.7%; Q2 improved to 5.8%; Q2 guidance reaffirmation implies ~6+%.
2. GAAP reported vs adjusted gap: SBC and intangible amortisation increase
   faster; adjusted EPS can compound double-digit while GAAP EPS lags.
3. Rising interest expense and D&A reduce GAAP earnings even with flat
   EBITDA. FY26 interest guidance $190–200M and total D&A ~$340M are
   headwinds to retained earnings.
4. Insurance-cycle moderation: if P&C premiums fall, insurer cost-cutting
   may slow data purchases.
5. AI disruption of data content economics: insurers may ask for AI
   “self-service” and resist paying data premium adds.
6. Balance-sheet flexibility: if buybacks continue while net debt rises,
   downgrade risk or equity reinvestment risk appears.
7. Customer consolidation among large P&C carriers — the per-installed-base
   risk.

Catalysts:
1. Q3/Q4 2026 reports confirming OCC revenue 6%+ and evidence that
   “growth returning to Investor Day targets” is material (company
   language, Q2-2026 release).
2. FY2027 guidance issued in Feb 2027 with 6–8% organic and 56.5%+ margin.
3. AI-product ARR disclosures or module attach-rate data.
4. Continued share-count shrink: if they complete the ASR at an average
